doc.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Hearing his clarinet on a live all-clarinet album
summary: Rowe plays a clarinet track; Collette comments on his clarinet influences and range of styles.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: I had one more little selection here. This is quite different I thought, and I noticed — see if you recognize this.
[audio interlude]
One of the many sessions you’ve done, this is all clarinets, with Hamiet Bluitt.
Yeah, some of these things I’ve never heard.
You’ve never heard them, yeah?
Well maybe when we recorded them.
I think that’s you right there. The notation on the album wasn’t quite sure.
That’s me, right. I kind of know the way I sound, at least I used to. It’s good to hear that because I don’t listen as much now.
Do you listen to your own music at home?
No.
Well you should, I think you’re pretty good.
Well thank you. Well to tell you the truth, nowadays I hear that playing and I’m just wondering, boy that was much better than I thought.
Well that particular album was pretty experimental I think, if I recall.
It had some good players on there.
Yeah. It was a live concert, wasn’t it?
Yes. It was a live concert. Mostly what you’ve got is a young guy, he’s playing good now?
Byron?
Yeah.
I can’t recall.
Was the first name Byron or last name Byron?
His last name is Byron.
He plays a lot of the Klezmer stuff too.
Well that just kind of shows how many different areas you’ve been into.

Oh yeah, lots of things. But yeah, that did sound pretty good. That was my approach to the clarinet. It’s different in a sense but I don’t know, but I’m drawing from a lot of different areas, you’re right. Naturally I heard Goodman and Shaw and all those guys, and Barney Bigard and Jimmy Hamilton. You put all that together and you’ve got a big span of sounds. And then doing a lot of the classical stuff too.
